children: Overview
Canada senior housing provider's Q3 revenue rose 12.4% yr/yr, driven by rental rate increases and acquisitions
Same-property NOI grew 8.7% yr/yr, with both retirement and LTC segments contributing
Adjusted FFO per share rose 5.2% yr/yr; company closed or contracted C$433 mln in 2026 acquisitions
Outlook
Sienna expects 2026 retirement segment Same Property NOI growth to exceed 10%
Company targets 2026 retirement occupancy of about 95% and margin growth of 150-200 bps
Sienna expects 2026 LTC Same Property NOI growth in the high-single-digit percentage range
Result Drivers
RENTAL RATE INCREASES AND ACQUISITIONS - Co said Q3 revenue growth in the retirement segment was mainly due to higher rental rates, acquisitions, and increased care and ancillary revenue

GOVERNMENT FUNDING AND PRIVATE ACCOMMODATION - Co said Q3 LTC segment revenue growth was mainly due to acquisitions, redevelopments, government funding increases, and higher private accommodation revenue
CONSTRUCTION FUNDING INCOME - Co said Q3 AFFO growth was partly driven by construction funding income received from the Government of Ontario for redevelopments completed in 2025
